title: Aunt Mattie, Captain Baker and his father's shipbuilding in Alabama
summary: Asked about early music interest, Jones introduces his aunt Mattie and recalls his father working for Captain Baker on the Warrior River and diving without a suit.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: That's most interesting. What is your first recollection of your great interest in music? When did you first begin to get a feeling for music, an interest?
I had an aunt that just recently passed. She was a twin; her name was Agnes - I mean, was Mattie. This is on my mother's side of the family of about 9 children approximately.
Mattie. I always referred to her as sister Mattie because she had a twin and she took me at the time of convalescing, she took me at the time to hear the Ringling Brothers circus.
How old were you about then, Jo?
I was convalescing. I must have been about 5 or 6 or 7 years old - about 5 or 6, between 5 and 7.

I don't remember. I don't know whether it was - it could have been - I'm pretty sure it was in Alabama because they sent for my father to come to work on the Warrior River and there was a Captain Baker that asked for the service of my father. Captain Baker was the kind [Black]

of a person that later on that you heard about Fate Marlowe and all those people that worked on the Mississippi, like Captain Joe. He was Captain Baker. This was the fore-runner of a Keyser that went during World War II. He was that kind of a ship-builder but they asked for my father because my father -
Go ahead, what were you saying?

My father was the type of person when they had the diving suits, he didn't use a diving suit. He could go under water and stay 3 minutes without breathing. It was phenomenal. He could go on to a boat, a yacht, or what have you and he could come up without the diving suit. Those diving suits were very, very heavy. My father would just go right under the water, go in and fix up whatever happened.

So you had been to Alabama once before. This was when you were about 5 or 6 and your father died down there when you were about 16... He died in 1922, yes, that he died there, but you had made frequent trips to Alabama?

I had been traveling and traveling then. I don't know - as young as I was I could not distinguish geographically where exactly I was. But the basic things I do know because I re-traversed these places starting around after I got older to go back to try to recapitulate where was I and ask people in a town if they knew my father or if they knew what-have-you. A lot of records and things was gone.
